subject.title: fix(codex): keep OpenClaw exec when native surface has no environment (#92238)

question: Should direct Codex app-server turns with the native surface enabled but zero registered environments fall back to OpenClaw's existing policy-filtered `exec` and `process` tools?
rationale: The code and proof support the fix, but exposing a shell where the current Codex surface has none is an intentional execution-boundary choice that repository policy reserves for an area owner.

options.title: Approve bounded fallback
options.body: Accept OpenClaw `exec` and `process` as the authoritative fallback only for zero-environment direct turns, preserving all current policy and exclusion gates.

options.title: Require Codex environment instead
options.body: Keep OpenClaw shell names filtered and redesign direct turns to register a Codex execution environment before native shell tools are advertised.

options.title: Keep direct turns shell-less
options.body: Reject the fallback and document that direct Codex turns without a registered environment cannot execute shell commands.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded fallback
recommendation.body: Accept OpenClaw `exec` and `process` as the authoritative fallback only for zero-environment direct turns, preserving all current policy and exclusion gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the commit that introduced the complete app-server tool and environment boundary affected by this decision.
